title: A/R Summary: the customer name header reverses on its first click
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Three customers have open invoices and you want to reverse the name order on A/R Summary.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Three customers have open invoices on today's date: {Customer-A}, {Customer-B} and {Customer-C}; in name order they read {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-01 Alder, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-01 Birch and {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-01 Cedar.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the header of the customer name column (the first column).
  2. Click the header of the customer name column (the first column) again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the list was already sorted by name, so this first click reverses it: Z to A, {Customer-C} above {Customer-B} above {Customer-A}.
  • Step 2: back to A to Z: {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C}.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R1, A/R Summary and A/P Summary columns: “A/R Summary and A/P Summary: the name column, Location (when shown), Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 91 And Over, Total.”
  • S2-R1: “Every column on all six reports sorts when its header is clicked, except A/P Unpaid Invoices' Vendor Name column (S2-N1). The columns are:”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”
  • S2-R3: “A header that is already the sorted column reverses on its first click.”
